Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
PICKING STICKS (ARMS) FOR OVERPICK JUTE LOOMS 

(First Revision) 



I. Material — As agreed to between the buyer and the seller; the picking sticks shall be made of 
natural wood or solid compressed wood or compressed laminated wood. 



2* Shape and Dimensions — See Fig. I and 2.

FIG. 2 TYPICAL DOUBLE GROOVE PICKING STICKS FOR OVERPICK JUTE LOOMS, TYPE 2 



3* Workmanship and Finish 

3.1 The natural wood for the manufacture of picking sticks shall be fully-seasoned [see IS : 1 1 4 1 - 1 958 

'Code of practice for seasoning of timbers (tentative)'] before use. 



Adopted 25 August 1970 



© April 1971, BIS 



Gr 1 



BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 



IS: 698- 1970 

3.2 The picking sticks shall be free from visible defects, such as checks, splits, gum veins, bark pockets, 
holes or any other defect which is likely to affect the life or usefulness of the picking sticks. [For the 
description of defects, see IS : 707-1969 ' Glossary of terms applicable to timber and timber products (first 
revision)']. 

3.3 The surface shall be sanded smooth. 

3.4 If an agreement between the buyer and the seller so provides, the picking sticks made of natural 
wood shall be soaked in either linseed oil (raw); groundnut oil, mineral oil (spindle oil) or sperm oil 
immediately after manufacture for a period of 12 hours and then allowed to stand for another 12 hours to 
drain off excess oil. 

4. Atmospheric Conditions for Conditioning and Testing — In case of dispute or if agreed to between 
the buyer and the seller the test sample shall be conditioned to moisture equilibrium and tested in the 
standard atmospheric conditions, that is, 65 db 2 percent relative humidity and 27 dfc 2°C temperature 
[see also IS : 196-1966 'Atmospheric conditions for testing (revised) 9 ]. 

5. Marking — Mark each picking stick at a suitable place with the manufacturer's name, initials or 
trade-mark. 

5.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

6. Packing — As agreed ta between the buyer and the seller. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
